name: Temporal Equivalence Principle: A Unified Resolution to the JWST High-Redshift Anomalies
description: JWST has revealed a pattern of high-redshift anomalies—such as extreme star formation efficiencies and unexpected stellar-to-dynamical mass ratios—that appear preferentially in deep gravitational potentials. This work tests whether these tensions can be resolved by relaxing the assumption of universal cosmic time. Under the Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP)—a continuously screened two-metric framework—proper time depends on the local environment in unscreened halos. Using a prespecified magnitude-sector benchmark (κ_gal = 0.960 × 10⁶ mag, Paper 11) applied without any JWST-specific parameter refitting, this framework quantitatively accounts for the leading photometric excesses; the factor ~ 2.4 residual between the canonical benchmark and the independent empirical Cepheid-channel recovery is stated explicitly and propagated through the prior range rather than tuned away. To address mass-proxy circularity, the framework is tested against kinematic data using the JWST-SUSPENSE survey (N=15) and a broader velocity dispersion (σ)-based expansion (N=75). In the SUSPENSE sample, the dynamical mass-to-light inference response (R_ML) retains residual spectral-age information after controlling for stellar mass and redshift (ρ = +0.556, p = 0.032), whereas stellar mass loses its predictive power once R_ML is controlled (ρ = +0.031, p = 0.91) — a suggestive one-sided asymmetry at N=15, pending replication, since the direct predictor comparison remains non-significant. The broader N=75 expansion is mixed: the σ-only R_ML adds no predictive power for M_beyond σ and z (partial ρ = +0.079, p = 0.50), and the sign of the residual-z trend is construction-dependent — opposite to expectation in the absorption-line subsample only under a σ-to-halo map that embeds expanding-cosmology virial drift, while the predicted sign is recovered under a cosmology-free σ-to-depth construction. The pooled trend is in any case a between-survey composition effect rather than a uniform within-survey signal. In large-sample photometry (N = 1,254 across three surveys), dust emergence and apparent evolutionary advance align strongly with potential depth (ρ = +0.635 at z > 8), organizing more cleanly along an effective-time coordinate than raw cosmic time. A secondary photometric test confirms that R_ML carries sSFR information beyond mass and redshift (ρ(R_ML, sSFR mid M_, z) = -0.62, p = 8.2 × 10⁻²⁹), with the negative sign predicted by the TEP measurement equations ( sSFR_obs ∝ R_ML^m-n_SPS with m 8 galaxy's ambient field, and with the DR4 lens-model magnification and cluster-centric distance in the baseline (+34.2), no same-epoch density proxy adds evidence (-7.1 on the full observable set, -6.0 on the physical subset). The comparison is interpreted as channel consistency with the operative ambient-field response law, not functional-form discrimination of the instantiated magnitude-sector kernel, and is treated as supportive context alongside the kinematic comparisons and the photometric correlation structure, positioning TEP as a coherent and falsifiable organizing framework for high-redshift galaxy evolution.
